summary: Round eleven delta reviewed: the absent-LINE guard in scripts/coverage.py, the two new CoverageGateTest cases, and the two backlog rows. Nothing blocking or major. The LINE/BRANCH asymmetry is sound: reproduced the -g:none report shape (INSTRUCTION+BRANCH, no LINE) against the real coverage.py and it exits 1 with a named remedy; nothing in buildSrc/src/main/kotlin or build.gradle.kts turns debug info off, so there is no false-fail path in this tree. Both new tests kill their named mutations by construction. Two minors recorded, neither to be fixed under review.md rule 11.

findings.title: M0.42 states a verified test count that this same commit made stale
findings.failure_scenario: The row claims 'delete the clause and all 14 CoverageGateTest cases stay green'. The file now holds 17 @Test methods, two of them added in this commit. The substance still holds (neither new fixture nests a module two levels deep, so the p.count('/') == 1 clause remains uncovered), but a reader auditing the claim counts 17, cannot reconcile it with 14, and has to re-derive whether the row is describing today's tree or a prior round. A number stated as verified and then left behind is the shape of a claim nobody re-ran.

findings.title: the new LINE guard precedes the exclusion check, so a baselined module cannot be excused from it
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced: a module with classes, a report carrying INSTRUCTION and BRANCH but no LINE, and a well-formed 'format  no product code yet; M1 lands the SPI' entry in baselines/coverage.txt exits 1 and never prints its EXCLUDED line. This is the same asymmetry M0.44 records for the missing-report path (missing.append runs before m in skips), but M0.44's wording names only the absent-report case, so the absent-LINE case is not covered by the row a future reader would consult. It fails closed and is consistent with the c == {} and c is None guards that already precede skips, so it is not a defect in behaviour -- only in what the backlog says is known.
